name: ESP32
description: Espressif ESP32 (ESP32-D0WD-V3, chip revision v3.1): two Xtensa LX6 cores at up to 240 MHz, 520 KiB of SRAM, 448 KiB of ROM, 16 KiB of RTC memory, external SPI flash behind the cores' caches, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; the ESP32-DevKitC's MCU. Espressif's ROM, ESP-IDF's second-stage bootloader and ESP-IDF applications run on both cores; the radios are not yet modelled.

memory.name: rom
memory.doc: Internal ROM0 (384 KiB) and ROM1 (64 KiB) on the instruction bus (TRM v5 table 3.3-1, ESP-IDF's SOC_IROM_MASK_HIGH 0x40070000): the boot ROM of chip revision v3, its image made by tools/importers/esprom.py (--base 0x40000000 --size 0x70000 --data-table 0x4000D4EC:0x4000D4F8, the Bluetooth controller's entry; --data-table 0x4000D4F8:0x4000D5C8, the ROM's copy table of its RAM variables' initial values) from Espressif's esp32_rev300_rom.elf (espressif/esp-rom-elfs 20241011, Apache-2.0: LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt; the ROM's code is Copyright (c) 2015-2022 Espressif Systems (Shanghai) Co. Ltd.). It equals byte for byte the image Espressif's QEMU loads (esp32-v3-rom.bin, sha256 9115bbcd...258b) over its 455,722 bytes; the rest reads zeros

memory.name: rom1_data
memory.doc: Internal ROM1 on the data bus

memory.name: sram0
memory.doc: Internal SRAM0 on the instruction bus: its first 64 KiB the cores' flash caches once they are enabled, the rest IRAM

memory.name: sram2
memory.doc: Internal SRAM2 on the data bus (DRAM)

memory.name: sram1
memory.doc: Internal SRAM1 on the data bus (DRAM), where the ROM keeps its data and stacks

memory.name: rtc_fast
memory.doc: RTC FAST memory on the data bus, kept in deep sleep

memory.name: rtc_fast_ibus
memory.doc: RTC FAST memory on the instruction bus

memory.name: rtc_slow
memory.doc: RTC SLOW memory, kept in deep sleep, the ULP coprocessor's

memory.name: flash
memory.doc: The module's 4 MB SPI flash, reached through SPI0 and SPI1 and read in place through the caches

memory.name: flash_drom
memory.doc: The data bus's window on the flash (DROM0, TRM table 3.3-3): 64 pages of 64 KB that MMU entries 0-63 map

memory.name: flash_irom
memory.doc: The instruction bus's window on the flash (IROM0 from the first whole page after RTC FAST memory to 0x403FFFFF): MMU entries 77-127

sources.name: xtal
sources.doc: The module's 40 MHz crystal (XTL_CLK); the CPU runs from it out of reset

sources.name: rc_fast
sources.doc: The internal 8 MHz RC oscillator (RC_FAST_CLK, 8MD256 its /256)

sources.name: rc_slow
sources.doc: The internal 150 kHz RC oscillator (RTC_SLOW_CLK's default)

sources.name: pll
sources.doc: PLL_CLK, 320 MHz (or 480 MHz) from the crystal

functional.claims: The two Xtensa LX6 cores (mcu/xtensa/lx6.c, lx6fp.c) as Espressif's core-isa.h configures them: the core and density instructions, the windowed registers (64, the overflow check of every instruction, CALL4/8/12, ENTRY, RETW and its underflow, MOVSP, ROTW, L32E/S32E), zero-overhead loops, MUL16/MULL/MULUH/MULSH, QUOS/QUOU/REMS/REMU, NSA, MIN/MAX, SEXT, CLAMPS, booleans, S32C1I with SCOMPARE1, THREADPTR, MISC0-3, PRID (0xCDCD, 0xABAB), the MAC16 package, the single-precision FPU (IEEE rounding modes and flags; the division and square root sequences libgcc runs give correctly rounded results), XEA2 exceptions with relocatable vectors, 32 interrupts at core-isa.h's levels and types (level, edge, software, the CCOMPARE0-2 timers against CCOUNT, NMI), RSIL, WAITI, RFI, the debug option's BREAK, IBREAK, DBREAK and ICOUNT, region protection (eight 512 MB regions, 15 no access), unaligned loads and stores, and the instruction bus's 32-bit-only data accesses. Both cores share the machine, the APP_CPU held in reset until DPORT releases it and seeing the ROM with its pointers into the PRO_CPU's ROM data moved to its own, as Espressif's own APP_CPU ROM image has them. The boot: Espressif's ROM (esp32_rev300_rom.elf, chip revision v3) from the reset vector, its banner, the strapping pins (GPIO_STRAP: SPI_FAST_FLASH_BOOT, or the download mode with GPIO0 low), the reset causes (RTC_CNTL), the eFuse glitch check, the flash read through SPI1, ESP-IDF's second-stage bootloader and its image check on the SHA accelerator, the caches' flash MMU, and the application on both cores. The models: DPORT (the APP_CPU's reset, clock and stall, CPU_PER_CONF, the caches' flush and state, the flash MMU tables, the interrupt matrix's 69 sources, the cross-CPU interrupts), RTC_CNTL (reset causes, the RTC timer, the RTC watchdog with its flash-boot protection, the software resets and stalls, the store registers, SOC_CLK_SEL), APB_CTRL (the CPU and APB clocks from XTAL, PLL or RC_FAST), the eFuse controller with the chip's factory bits (ESP32-D0WD-V3 v3.1, a MAC with its CRC, or the board settings'), GPIO and IO_MUX (40 pads, the matrix, pulls, open drain, interrupts on each CPU, the strapping latch), UART0-2 (FIFOs, frames at the baud rate, interrupts), TIMG0/1 (T0, T1, the LAC timer, the MWDT with its flash-boot protection, the RTC_SLOW_CLK calibration), SPI0/SPI1 with the module's Giantec GT25Q32A flash (C4 60 16, the ID the owner's board reports), the SHA accelerator (SHA-1, -256, -384, -512), the internal analog I2C master, the random number generator and the peripherals' AHB view.
omissions: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the RF front end (WIFI_MAC, BB, NRX, FE: their registers keep what is written)

the double-precision accelerator's instructions (F64ADDC, F64ITER and the others: their encodings are public, not what they do; a program that runs one stops with a diagnostic), though its registers are kept
PSRAM (DRAM1), the boot remap, the APB/AHB access permissions, the caches' lock regions and timing (the mapped pages are read whole), the MMU's access-error interrupts

the peripherals without a model yet: I2C0/1, I2S0/1, SPI2/3 (HSPI, VSPI), RMT, LEDC, MCPWM, PCNT, TWAI, SDMMC, EMAC, the SAR ADCs, the DACs, the touch sensor, the RTC IO MUX and the ULP coprocessor, the AES and RSA accelerators, flash encryption
sleep modes (light and deep sleep, the power domains), brown-out
the eFuse 3/4 coding scheme's check, BLOCK0's per-field write protection
validation: tests/unit/test_lx6.c: programs assembled by Espressif's assembler (integer, shifts, multiply and divide, loops, branches, memory with S32C1I, windowed recursion through the ROM's own window vectors, SYSCALL, the CCOMPARE timer interrupt, FPU, MAC16), and the APP_CPU's ROM data kept apart
tests/vendor/esp-idf: ESP-IDF v5.4's hello_world built unmodified for the esp32 target on the ESP32-DevKitC V4, from the ROM's banner to esp_restart
the ROM image equals Espressif QEMU's esp32-v3-rom.bin byte for byte, and the APP_CPU's view of it QEMU's esp32-v3-rom-app.bin

timed.claims: Instruction timing estimated: one cycle, a taken branch, jump, call or return three, MULL two, a division twelve, an exception's entry three; CCOUNT counts those cycles. The clocks follow the registers: CPU_CLK from XTAL (40 MHz out of reset), the PLL's 80, 160 or 240 MHz, or RC_FAST; APB_CLK; RTC_SLOW_CLK at the RC oscillator's nominal 150 kHz.
omissions: the LX6 pipeline's interlocks and the loop buffer's timing
cache misses and flash latency (the SPI transfers' bus time is counted on SPI1, the flash's own program and erase times too)
the RC oscillators' error and drift

electrical.claims: GPIO pin-model defaults at 3.3 V from the datasheet's DC characteristics: VIH 0.75 VDD, VIL 0.25 VDD, VOH 0.8 VDD, VOL 0.1 VDD, 45 kOhm pulls; GPIO34-39 inputs only.
omissions: the supply current (the datasheet's power modes are not yet in the description)
